Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to migrate their data and settings from an existing app to a designated replacement app. Details below.

iOS to Make App Replacement Easier

While it doesn't happen often, developers will occasionally retire an existing app and introduce a new one to replace it, requiring users to transition to a different standalone app.

Even though most developers try to make the transition as seamless as possible, migration may still require user intervention, particularly when it comes to data that isn't stored in the cloud.

With the launch of iOS 27.2, Apple is addressing this issue through a new system-managed migration flow that can transfer an app's data and supported settings to its designated replacement before the old app is deleted.

Based on existing code in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will see the following alert:

The developer suggests moving your data and settings from your existing "%1$@" app to the new "%2$@" app. iPhone can now do this for you before you start using the new app. When finished, the old app will be deleted from this iPhone.

Users will then have the option to choose "Move App Data & Settings" or "Don't Move Anything." If a user declines the migration, iOS will display a second confirmation warning, noting that some preferences (including notification and location settings) might need to be reconfigured.

To be clear, this feature appears to be limited to situations where a developer replaces their own app with a designated successor, rather than migrating data between apps owned by different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a number of system-level settings and permissions, including:

  • Privacy, Location, and Health authorizations
  • Notification settings, including accessory notification settings
  • Per-app Do Not Disturb and Focus settings
  • App Lock and Protected settings
  • CarPlay icon arrangement and compatible widget layouts
  • Live Activities and accessory Live Activities
  • Access rights for relevant accessories
  • LaunchServices preferences, fonts, capture-related defaults, phone data, and Secure Element services

We'll be keeping a close eye on changes to this framework throughout the iOS 27.2 beta testing period, and will report back as we learn more about how developers implement this feature.
